title: Building a Gimbal That Shows Rotation Losing a Dimension
concept_layer: rotation as angular transformation; Euler angles; gimbal lock; why quaternions exist

capture_leaks.non_commutativity: Rx·Ry ≠ Ry·Rx — Euler rotations don't compose like translations. This map hints; Trans_Composition answers.
capture_leaks.gimbal_lock: Euler angles lose a degree of freedom when two axes align. The map demonstrates it; quaternions in wavefunctions repair it.
capture_leaks.interpolation: You can't average two orientations with Euler angles — quaternions or rotation matrices needed.
capture_leaks.continuous_rotation: 360 ≡ 0 — angles wrap. This breaks naive distance metrics on SO(3); addressed in softbodies/ML.

limit: Three sliders control three axes. Looks clean — until two axes merge into one. The gimbal teaches why rotation is not three independent numbers. Orientation lives on a curved manifold that Euler angles cannot chart without singularities.

stages.title: From displacement to orientation
stages.thinking: In Trans_Translation you learned translation requires direction and magnitude — a vector added to position. Now a new question: if a form can move through space, can it also turn? Translation changes where. Rotation changes which way. Same object, different world.
stages.code:
# Translation — what you learned:
var position: Vector3 = Vector3(0, 0, 0)
position += Vector3(1, 0, 0)  # moves right

# Rotation — the new question:
# How do you store "which way am I facing"?
# Three angles? A matrix? A quaternion?
# This map starts with the obvious answer — three angles —
# and shows you why that answer is not enough.

var angle_x: float = 0.0  # pitch
var angle_y: float = 0.0  # yaw
var angle_z: float = 0.0  # roll

stages.title: Three nested rings
stages.thinking: The physical mechanism is old — ships, telescopes, cameras have used it for centuries. Three rings, each free to spin on one axis, nested inside each other. The outermost ring holds the next, which holds the next, which holds the object. Each Euler angle drives one ring. This is the literal meaning of 'gimbal.'
stages.code:
extends Node3D
class_name RotationGimbal

func _build_gimbal() -> void:
	_gimbal_root = Node3D.new()
	add_child(_gimbal_root)
	
	# Outer: X-axis ring (red, pitch)
	_x_ring_pivot = Node3D.new()
	_gimbal_root.add_child(_x_ring_pivot)
	_x_ring = _create_ring(ring_radius_outer, color_x, "XRing")
	_x_ring_pivot.add_child(_x_ring)
	
	# Middle: Y-axis ring (green, yaw), child of X
	_y_ring_pivot = Node3D.new()
	_x_ring_pivot.add_child(_y_ring_pivot)
	_y_ring = _create_ring(ring_radius_mid, color_y, "YRing")
	_y_ring.rotation_degrees.z = 90.0  # align torus with Y axis
	_y_ring_pivot.add_child(_y_ring)
	
	# Inner: Z-axis ring (blue, roll), child of Y
	_z_ring_pivot = Node3D.new()
	_y_ring_pivot.add_child(_z_ring_pivot)
	_z_ring = _create_ring(ring_radius_inner, color_z, "ZRing")
	_z_ring.rotation_degrees.x = 90.0
	_z_ring_pivot.add_child(_z_ring)

stages.title: Each ring is a torus, glowing
stages.thinking: TorusMesh is new here — inner_radius and outer_radius define a ring shape. The three rings are color-coded by axis: red = X (pitch), green = Y (yaw), blue = Z (roll). Emission energy so they remain visible when rotated edge-on. Semi-transparent so the inner structure reads through.
stages.code:
func _create_ring(radius: float, tube_radius: float, color: Color, ring_name: String) -> MeshInstance3D:
	var ring = MeshInstance3D.new()
	ring.name = ring_name
	var torus = TorusMesh.new()
	torus.inner_radius = radius - tube_radius
	torus.outer_radius = radius + tube_radius
	torus.rings = 32
	torus.ring_segments = 24
	ring.mesh = torus
	
	var mat = StandardMaterial3D.new()
	mat.albedo_color = Color(color, 0.85)
	mat.emission_enabled = true
	mat.emission = color
	mat.emission_energy_multiplier = 0.6
	mat.transparency = BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA
	ring.material_override = mat
	return ring

stages.title: Apply the Euler triple
stages.thinking: Three sliders drive three rings. Each ring rotates only on its own axis. Because the rings are nested, each rotation is applied in the frame of its parent — X first, then Y inside that, then Z inside that. This is the composition order Rx·Ry·Rz. A different nesting would give a different result from the same three numbers.
stages.code:
func _update_gimbal() -> void:
	# Euler composition order: X (outer) -> Y (middle) -> Z (inner)
	_x_ring_pivot.rotation_degrees = Vector3(angle_x, 0, 0)
	_y_ring_pivot.rotation_degrees = Vector3(0, angle_y, 0)
	_z_ring_pivot.rotation_degrees = Vector3(0, 0, angle_z)
	
	# The inner box (child of Z pivot) inherits all three rotations
	# via the parent chain — this is the final orientation.
	
	_check_gimbal_lock()
	_update_angles_label()
	_update_matrix_label()

stages.title: Build the combined matrix
stages.thinking: The three angles compose into a single 3x3 rotation matrix. Rx(α)·Ry(β)·Rz(γ) expands to nine entries of sines and cosines. The label shows the live matrix. Watch the entries change as sliders move — the matrix IS the orientation, the angles are just one way to reach it.

stages.title: Detect the singularity
stages.thinking: The critical moment: when Y approaches ±90°, the X and Z axes point in the same direction in world space. Moving the X slider or the Z slider now does the SAME thing. One degree of freedom vanishes. This is gimbal lock. The detection is simple — measure distance to 90° modulo 360 — but what it reveals is that Euler angles cannot chart all orientations smoothly.

stages.title: Make the loss felt
stages.thinking: Detection is not teaching. When lock happens, the warning flashes, the outer rings pulse, the info text changes. The player isn’t told Euler is insufficient — they feel it. They slide X, the box doesn’t twist the way they expect. They slide Z, same thing. Two controls, one response. The body learns before the mind names it.

stages.title: Give it identity
stages.thinking: The gimbal knows what it is. It is not a widget that rotates a box. It is a physical demonstration that rotation cannot be parameterized by three numbers without singularities. Gimbal lock is not a bug to fix inside this map. It is the lesson. Quaternions exist because this map is true.
stages.code:
# @identity
# essence: three nested rings driven by Euler angles; when middle angle → ±90°, outer and inner axes align and collapse to one
# desire: learner feels rotation as a curved space that Euler angles cannot chart smoothly
# critical_parameter: angle_y — at ±90° the gimbal locks; at other values, three independent rotations
# triggers: Y slider approaching 90° flashes GIMBAL LOCK, pulses X/Z rings, collapses X and Z into the same axis
# emerges: the need for quaternions; the topology of SO(3); the non-commutativity of rotation
# needs: 3 angle sliders [has]; rotation matrix display [has]; lock-warning label [has]
# relationships: extends Trans_Translation; demands what Trans_Composition composes; foreshadows wavefunctions (quaternion)
# truth: rotation lives on a curved manifold — three angles are a convenient but leaky chart
